hook: Internal Air Force Office of Special Investigations (AFOSI) email chain processing a declassification review of an IIR documenting a civilian's nighttime sighting of a large, blue triangular object near a national security facility in the Pacific Time Zone in March 2023.
why_it_matters: This document reveals the bureaucratic pathway by which a SECRET//NOFORN intelligence report on a UAP sighting is converted into an unclassified product — specifically a 'derivative classification review' rather than a full declassification, which required only HQ concurrence rather than AFOSI Commander signature. The embedded unclassified summary preserves first-person witness language about anomalous movement ('jerking,' 'jumping') inconsistent with known propulsion, observed near an unnamed national security facility. The involvement of the Office of the Undersecretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security as the requesting party suggests this sighting was flagged as significant enough to warrant cross-organizational disclosure coordination.

key_findings.finding: A civilian reported a large blue featureless triangular object hovering near a national security facility for approximately three minutes before moving erratically.

quotes.text: An individual reported observing a large blue featureless triangular object with a solid, unwavering silhouette emitting powerful "whitish blue" light from multiple points along its perimeter.
The reporter described the object as "hovering" stationary above or near a national security facility for approximately three minutes.

key_findings.finding: The object's movement was described as anomalous — non-smooth, jerking or jumping — inconsistent with conventional jet propulsion.

quotes.text: The reporter characterized the object's motion as "backing up" in a "jerking" or "jumping" manner inconsistent with "smooth" jet propulsion.

key_findings.finding: The reporter explicitly ruled out several conventional explanations, including drone identification, while also clarifying the object did not display cloaking, vapor trail, or data-collection capabilities.

quotes.text: They stated that "didn't think" the object was a drone.
They stated that the object did not seem to travel along a defined flight path, possess any "photograph or data collection capabilities," emit a "vapor trail," or demonstrate "cloaking capabilities."

key_findings.finding: The sighting evidence was captured on a personal cellular device, and the original IIR was classified SECRET//NOFORN before being processed for release as UNCLASSIFIED.

The declassification pathway used was a 'derivative classification review' — a novel approach for this official — avoiding the more burdensome full declassification process that requires AFOSI Commander signature.

quotes.text: Our process for declassifying IIRs is lengthy and requires AFOSI Commander signature so I'm exploring options akin to a security review of the UNCLASS summary you have provided below.
our folks confirmed we do have the authority to process this as a derivative classification review, instead of a declassification request.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This is a 2023 UAP IIR being processed through the modern DoD disclosure apparatus, with the Office of the Undersecretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security coordinating release — the same institutional structure that supports AARO's reporting mandate.

AFOSI (Air Force Office of Special Investigations), whose commander signature is required for full IIR declassification, is the Air Force counterintelligence arm historically based at Wright-Patterson and central to Air Force UAP collection.
